panels.rationale: Single H&E photomicrograph from the surgically excised specimen of a 72-year-old male patient with a thyroglossal duct cyst. The caption explicitly describes cyst tissue lined in areas by stratified squamous epithelium and, in the fibrocollagenous wall, thyroid follicles of various sizes filled with colloid; the in-text histopathology report confirms TDC with no malignant cells in this cohort. Ectopic colloid-filled thyroid follicles within the cyst wall are a classic diagnostic histologic feature of thyroglossal duct cyst, so disease attribution and finding identification are both strong. The squamous epithelial lining described in the caption is not covered by the offered respiratory-epithelial vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding rather than forcing an incorrect key. No panel labels or seams are present, so the figure is treated as one panel.

panels.rationale: Contrast-enhanced axial cervical CT from a case report of malignant thyroglossal duct cyst treated with the Sistrunk procedure. The off-midline right parasagittal location is a recognized less-common presentation, so typicality is variant. No panel letters appear in the image or caption; the four axial slices are presented as one radiology figure, so it is a single panel A. No clinical annotations (arrows/callouts) are present, only scanner text overlays. Age and ethnicity are not stated.

in_text_mentions: Excision of the cyst with the body of the hyoid bone and the track to the base of the tongue was performed. The specimen was sent for histopathologic examination. In a focal area of the cyst wall, there was a small portion of thyroid tissue (Fig. 2). The final pathologic diagnosis was a thyroglossal duct cyst. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and recurrence of the disease has not been seen for the past year.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Real patient H&E of the resected specimen; ectopic thyroid follicles in the fibrous cyst wall are the textbook diagnostic histology of a thyroglossal duct cyst and match the vocabulary finding directly. Article is disease-focused (mediastinal TGDC) and the in-text final diagnosis is benign mediastinal TGDC. [raw subtype: mediastinal] B: Real patient H&E of the same resected TGDC specimen showing the cyst epithelial lining (attenuated squamous-to-cuboidal), a recognized lining of TGDC. Not a diagram/control/other disease; the squamous-to-cuboidal lining is not the ciliated respiratory lining in the vocabulary, so it is captured as a proposed finding rather than misattributed to the respiratory-lining key. [raw subtype: mediastinal] C: Real patient H&E of the resected TGDC showing stratified keratinizing squamous epithelium lining the cyst, a recognized (less common) lining pattern for TGDC. panels.figure_caption: Histopathological examination of the resected specimen (haematoxylin and eosin stain). (A) Ectopic follicular thyroid tissue within the fibrous cyst wall. (B) Attenuated squamous-to-cuboidal epithelial lining. (C) Stratified keratinizing squamous epithelium. (D) Foreign-body giant-cell reaction and chronic inflammatory infiltrate. Original magnification ×40; scale bars = 500 micrometres.
in_text_mentions: Gross pathology showed a 16.5-g cystic specimen measuring 5 × 4 × 3.2 cm. Histology demonstrated a cyst lined predominantly by stratified squamous epithelium and focally by attenuated cuboidal/ columnar epithelium, with mature thyroid follicles in the fibrous cyst wall and a foreign-body giant-cell reaction (Fig. 4). There was no epithelial dysplasia or malignancy. The final diagnosis was a benign mediastinal TGDC.
